Great food in a lovely, classy restaurant
May 2026 • Couples
My wife and I had a wonderful meal at Link Bistro. The restaurant is part of a hotel, and therefore could be considered to be slightly pricier than other restaurants, but we felt the value for what we had was exceptional.

We had a seven course tasting menu, plus two glasses of wine each and a cocktail each, and it all came to less than £100. Still expensive by Vietnam standards, but a third of what it would cost for a similar standard meal in Europe.

The restaurant is nicely lit and tastefully decorated, and we were served by a wonderful waitress named Kim. She was polite, friendly, professional and attentive, and we received great service from her. She even wrote us a lovely note on a leaf as a momento, and she helped make the evening really special.

Unfortunately, the restaurant is very quiet (apparently it is usually quiet) and we were the only diners that evening, hence knocking a star off for atmosphere. There wasn't really an atmosphere, apart from the bar and waiting staff there wasn't anyone else to create an atmosphere.

I really don't understand why the restaurant is not more popular. It has universally excellent reviews, so it is a mystery why it is not more busy. I hope that my positive review will encourage others to eat here, because the food was excellent and it's a lovely place, and they deserve to be busier and more successful.

I must say, I was truly impressed by everything they created for us.
I had pre-ordered three appetizers: a bun cha-style salad, abalone spring rolls, and a curly lettuce salad. For the main course, we all chose seabass and salmon. For dessert, we ordered two portions of coconut cake served with crispy peanut candy.

I was particularly impressed right from the beginning when Chef Kiet personally came to introduce their homemade sourdough bread, fermented for 100 hours such dedication! It was served with house-made butter, which was absolutely delightful.
At the end of the meal, we were pleasantly surprised with three complimentary drinks called “Gracias” as a thank-you gesture. I truly loved the way they presented this even though it was complimentary, it was crafted with great care and attention to detail. The bartender came to our table, skillfully shaking the drinks and finishing by flaming an orange peel right in front of us a wonderful sensory experience.
By the end of the evening, we felt like we had just enjoyed not only a meal, but a full performance.
This is definitely a restaurant everyone should experience at least once.
